01.actor: Ravina and Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti
01.event: While Ravina sat before Rabbi Yirmeya, a man walked past with his head uncovered and Ravina called him rude.
01.turn: Rabbi Yirmeya suggested the man might come from Mata Mehasya, where rabbis are so common that people are lax about showing honor.
01.outcome: Ravina's judgment is softened by the excuse; no further result is stated.
01.summary: Ravina was sitting before Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti when a man passed by with his head uncovered. Ravina said how rude the man was. Rabbi Yirmeya answered that he might be from Mata Mehasya, where rabbis are everywhere and people are not careful about such honor.

03.actor: a man who betrothed a woman conditionally, and the Sages
03.event: A man betrothed a woman on a condition, then had intercourse with her.
03.turn: The condition was unmet, but the Sages lacked the power to release her without a divorce document.
03.outcome: They made him give her a bill of divorce.
03.summary: The text says an actual incident occurred in which a man betrothed a woman conditionally and then had intercourse with her. The Sages could not declare the betrothal void, so they required him to give her a bill of divorce. It is told only briefly, as an illustration of a ruling.
03.missing: Names, the details of the condition, and how the incident played out are not given.

04.event: Sent to betroth a woman for his son, Ravin betrothed her to himself.
04.turn: This looked like deceit, which a baraita condemns; the explanation is that her family would not give her to the son, and Ravin feared someone else would take her while he reported back.
04.outcome: The betrothal stands, and his conduct is justified by the circumstances.
04.summary: Ravin the Pious went to arrange a betrothal for his son but ended up betrothing the woman to himself. Asked how a pious man could act so deceitfully, the answer is that her family refused the son and would give her only to the father. He did not go back to tell his son because someone else might have betrothed her in the meantime.

05.event: When people wanted to declare Babylonian lineage inferior, Pineḥas told his servants to carry him out on a stretcher after he spoke, then stated a decoy law and the true teaching in the study house.
05.turn: As the scholars examined his strange ruling, he said the lineage of all lands is muddled relative to Eretz Yisrael and Eretz Yisrael relative to Babylonia, and his servants ran off with him.
05.outcome: The scholars could not catch him; they investigated families until they reached powerful ones, found it dangerous, and gave up.
05.summary: When people sought to brand Babylonian lineage as inferior, Rabbi Pineḥas told his servants to carry him off on a stretcher the moment he spoke. In the study house he first stated a surprising law, and while they scrutinized it he declared the lineage teaching and was hurried away. His pursuers could not catch him, and their own inquiry into families stopped when it reached dangerously powerful ones.

06.actor: Abaye, Rav Safra and Rav Yosef
06.event: Rav Safra challenged Abaye's teaching with two mishnayot and Abaye answered the first, but was silent on the second.
06.turn: Abaye told Rav Yosef what Rav Safra had said, and Rav Yosef asked why he had not answered that members of a group are vigilant.
06.outcome: Rav Yosef gives the answer Abaye missed.
06.summary: Rav Safra raised objections against a teaching Abaye had recited. Abaye answered one but fell silent at the other, and later reported the exchange to Rav Yosef. Rav Yosef asked why he had not simply answered that members of a Passover group are vigilant.
06.missing: This is mainly a legal debate; only the silence and the report to Rav Yosef are event-like.

07.actor: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi (and Rabbi Tzadok)
07.event: A noblewoman tried to seduce Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi, and he made himself covered in boils by an incantation; she healed him by magic, so he fled to a dangerous bathhouse.
07.turn: The next day the Sages asked who protected him, and he said soldiers guarded him all night; they said a miracle happens to one who is saved from forbidden intercourse.
07.outcome: He was protected and the Sages explained it; a second story follows of Rabbi Tzadok escaping a noblewoman by sitting in an oven.
07.summary: A noblewoman tried to seduce Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi, and he used an incantation to cover himself with boils; she healed him with magic, and he fled to a bathhouse where people were usually harmed. In the morning he told the Sages that guards protected him all night, and they explained that a miracle happens for one who was saved from forbidden intercourse. A second noblewoman tried to entice Rabbi Tzadok, who feigned weakness, had her roast forbidden food, and sat in the oven to show the fate of one who sins, so she backed off.

08.actor: a man picking dates and a woman
08.event: A man picking dates offered to throw her two if she would be betrothed to him, and she said only 'throw, throw'.
08.turn: Her repeated phrase was not real acceptance.
08.outcome: Rav Zevid ruled she is not betrothed.
08.summary: A man was picking dates when a woman asked him to throw her two. He said he would if she agreed to be betrothed to him, and she answered only 'throw, throw'. Rav Zevid ruled that such an answer means nothing and she is not betrothed.

09.actor: the wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava, and Rav Neḥemya
09.event: She came before Rav Neḥemya asking for sustenance and wine.
09.turn: He granted the sustenance and, when she asked for wine, granted that too.
09.outcome: He awarded both, noting that the residents of Meḥoza drink wine.
09.summary: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava came before Rav Neḥemya and asked him to apportion sustenance for her, and he did. She then asked for wine, and he granted that as well, saying he knew the people of Meḥoza drink wine.

10.actor: Rava and a woman obligated to take an oath
10.event: A woman had to take an oath in Rava's court, and Rava's wife told him she knew the woman was untrustworthy about oaths.
10.outcome: He reversed the oath onto the other party.
10.summary: A woman was obligated to swear an oath in Rava's court. Rava's wife, the daughter of Rav Ḥisda, told him she knew the woman was suspect about oaths. Rava then turned the oath over to the opposing party.

11.actor: Rabbi Neḥemya and Rava, each approached by a poor man
11.event: A man came to Rabbi Neḥemya for charity and said he normally dined on fatty meat and aged wine, so Neḥemya invited him to eat lentils; separately, a man told Rava he ate fattened hen and old wine and claimed God supplied it.
11.turn: The first man ate lentils and died; the second was vindicated when Rava's sister arrived unexpectedly after thirteen years with a fattened hen and old wine.
11.outcome: Neḥemya blamed the man's pampering; Rava told the man he had responded to his claim and invited him to eat.
11.summary: A poor man used to fatty meat and aged wine came to Rabbi Neḥemya, ate lentils with him, and died, and Neḥemya said the man should not have pampered himself. Another man of the same kind came to Rava and argued that his food came from God, not the community. Just then Rava's sister, unseen for thirteen years, arrived with a fattened hen and old wine, and Rava told the man to eat.

12.actor: Mar Yehuda and Rav Huna bar Yehuda
12.event: Mar Yehuda visited Rav Huna's house and saw people carrying among trees not planted in rows.
12.turn: He asked whether Rav Huna did not follow Avimi's ruling.
12.outcome: Rav Huna replied that he follows Rav Naḥman, who permits it.
12.summary: Mar Yehuda came to the house of Rav Huna bar Yehuda and saw people carrying among trees not planted in rows. He asked if Rav Huna did not hold like Avimi. Rav Huna answered that he follows Rav Naḥman.

13.actor: the father of Shmuel and Rabbi Yehuda Nesia
13.event: A bill of divorce was found in Neharde'a naming Androlinai, and it was unclear if the husband was the man in question or another with the same name; Shmuel's father sent the question to Rabbi Yehuda Nesia.
13.turn: The reply came back that all of Neharde'a must be examined.
13.outcome: Abaye uses this as proof of concern about two men with one name.
13.summary: A bill of divorce was found in Neharde'a, and the woman wanted to remarry on its strength, but it was not clear whether another man shared the husband's name. The father of Shmuel sent the question to Rabbi Yehuda Nesia in Eretz Yisrael, who answered that all of Neharde'a should be examined.
13.missing: Whether the woman was permitted to remarry is not stated.

14.event: Rava boasted that he was like ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias, ready to answer anything, and a Sage asked how many apples are needed for an eiruv.
14.turn: Rava replied that one doesn't establish an eiruv with apples.
14.outcome: The Sage rebutted from a mishna that apples do count.
14.summary: In a good mood, Rava declared himself ready to answer any question like ben Azzai. A Sage asked him how many apples are needed for an eiruv, and Rava answered that one does not make an eiruv with apples. The Sage challenged him with a mishna showing that all foods count.

15.actor: Bonyam ben Nunyam and Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi)
15.event: Bonyam ben Nunyam sent Rabbi a gift of special fine linens.
15.summary: Rav Dimi reports that Bonyam ben Nunyam sent Rabbi a gift of four kinds of very fine linen, which folded down to the size of a nut or pistachio and could be unfolded to cover him.
15.missing: No turn or outcome; it only reports the gift and explains the fabrics.

17.actor: a man with a debt of 1000 dinars, his creditor, and the purchaser of his mansions
17.event: The man sold his two mansions for 500 each, the creditor repossessed one and then sought the other, and the purchaser took 1000 dinars to the creditor offering to keep the first or take the money and give up both.
17.turn: Rami bar Ḥama then compared it to a mishna and Rava distinguished it.
17.outcome: The creditor's response is not told; only how to write the repossession document is decided.
17.summary: A man owed his creditor 1000 dinars and sold two mansions for 500 each. The creditor repossessed one from the purchaser and then moved to take the other too. The purchaser took 1000 dinars to the creditor and said he could keep the first mansion if worth that to him, or take the money and give up both.
17.missing: What the creditor did is never stated; the rest is legal discussion.

18.actor: a man, a woman washing her feet, and Rava
18.event: A man grabbed dinars from another person, threw them to a woman washing her feet, and said she was betrothed to him.
18.turn: He came before Rava to ask about her status.
18.outcome: Rava ruled the money was stolen, so the betrothal had no effect.
18.summary: A woman was washing her feet when a man snatched coins from someone else, threw them to her, and declared her betrothed. He then asked Rava about it. Rava ruled that since the owner had not given up on the money, the betrothal was invalid.

19.actor: a husband, his first wife, and Rava
19.event: A woman brought two maidservants to her husband, he married a second woman and gave her one of the maidservants.
19.turn: The first wife came before Rava and cried out.
19.outcome: Rava took no notice of her; the reason was that the house benefited.
19.summary: A woman brought her husband two maidservants as part of her property. He married another woman and brought one maidservant to her. The first wife came before Rava and wept, but Rava ignored her complaint.

20.event: Rav Yosef said he had not heard a ruling, and his student Abaye reminded him he had told it to them.
20.turn: Abaye cited the mishna and Rav Yehuda's statement in Rav's name.
20.outcome: The reminder is stated and the matter continues in debate.
20.summary: Rav Yosef said he did not remember hearing a certain ruling. His student Abaye told him that he himself had taught it, and cited the mishna and Rav Yehuda's report in Rav's name.
20.missing: It is a scholarly exchange more than a story; the outcome is not narrated.
